subject: spanish

items.correct: Yes — they agree with the noun's gender and number (rojo/roja/rojos/rojas).
items.why: Adjectives must match the noun they describe.

items.q: Are all Spanish nouns ending in -o masculine and -a feminine?
items.correct: It's a useful guide, but there are exceptions (el día, la mano, el problema).
items.why: Most follow the pattern, but common exceptions must be learned.

items.q: Do 'ser' and 'estar' mean the same and swap freely?
items.correct: No — ser is for permanent/identity, estar for states and location.
items.why: Choosing the wrong one can change the meaning of a sentence.

items.q: Can you translate English into Spanish word-for-word?
items.correct: No — word order and structures differ (adjectives usually follow the noun).
items.random_wrong: Spanish has the exact grammar of English.
items.why: Literal translation often produces errors and false friends.
